description:
From the fz-kdt.178 cold review (2026-09-03, 0889c0b3a). callsite_dispatch.rs
covers(early, late) asks every position "either the tests separate here, or
early's surface contains late's here" with an `all` -- so a pair whose tests
are DISJOINT at subject 0 (no value can satisfy both arms at all) is still
judged blind at subject 1 where their list tails overlap, and the seat is
told it owes coverage for a routing that routes nothing. The static census
reader (drive_test.rs blind_escapes / covers) mirrors production exactly and
so reports the same fiction. Measured once the census walked wrapper
selection plans: 00277 wrapper w13 arm 4 (s0 = :tail, s1 = [:tail]) vs arm 9
(s0 = int, s1 = [int] | [int | :tail]) -- :tail and int cannot overlap, yet
"arm 9 covers arm 4, seated second" is reported. ARM_ORDER_CENSUS: 65 blind =
28 unreachable-pair + 37 reachable; 62 seat findings = 28 + 34; corpus 73 =
28 + 45. It never showed while the walk saw only single-subject call edges.
FIX: a pair is a seat question only if some value can satisfy BOTH arms'
tests -- `overlaps` across all positions (the predicate already exists:
RuntimeTypePredicate::overlaps) is the precondition; a disjoint pair is
neither blind nor covering, it is separated, and the seat may leave it as it
arrived. Production and the census reader change together (one relation, two
readers). Red-first: the w13 arm 4 / arm 9 pair as a unit CallSiteSummary
(seats_before must be false both ways and the pair must not count as a
blind escape); the census constants drop by exactly 28. Sequence: before
fz-kdt.179 (so 179's reproducer is the 34 reachable seats, not 62).

comments.text: MEASURED AND PINNED (fz-kdt.178, 8de517a28). BLIND_ESCAPE_UNREACHABLE_PAIRS holds all 28 on 00277 w13-w19 (4 each): subject 0 asks a :tail head against an int head, which no value answers both ways, while subject 1 is the list behind it that no test reads. The census reader's separated_somewhere uses RuntimeTypePredicate::overlaps and mirrors production's covers exactly, so both readers change together. Two more facts for the fix: (a) under arms:6, enum_predicate_search's `[int | :nil] with [int]` at executable 201 is ALSO an unreachable pair, so one of fz-kdt.131's two seed-6 facet-3 pairs is fiction and only the executable-203 pair is real; (b) the refuter measured 00420_enum_take_drop_split and behavior/enum_take_drop_split at 0 unreachable-pair readings (the first cut's "215" did not exist); they are in the census with 4 reachable seat findings each, so the corpus's 45 reachable seat findings are all pinned. Sequence: before fz-kdt.179.

title: covers judges each position with an all: a pair whose tests are DISJOINT at one position is still called blind at another, so 28 of 62 selection seat findings on 00277 are pairs no value can reach
